messages:
release-manager: Cutting canary v2.3.1 now, but deploybot flagged a CI failure on the artifact job. holding promotion.
deploybot: Promotion blocked: staging -> canary. Reason: cache-restore-thundering-herd error on artifact-uploader (see logs).
release-manager: Ugh. @marta can you triage? this blocks the canary window.
marta: looking. saw some S3 503s in the uploader task but also a cache checksum mismatch for wheel:
```
Checksum mismatch: expected 2d7a4f, got 9b3c11 for wheel-redwood-serving-0.12.3.whl
Uploader returned 500 after retrying multipart parts
```
marta: I think two things happened: multipart upload retried and left partial state, then cache restore retried and read a wrong manifest.
jas: if it's a manifest/cached blob mismatch we should pin to the last known-good artifact and promote that instead of forcing a rebuild during the change window.
akira: +1 to pin. Rebuilding will re-run the flaky uploader and could tie up infra. Which tag is last good?
theo: last green promote was 3838950000 with image tag release-2.3.0-20260315. I can open a quick promote of that tag to canary if we decide to pin.
marta: I can also try clearing partial multipart uploads for the bucket and re-run the artifact job, but that takes ~20 mins and might still flake.
release-manager: Two options: A) pin to release-2.3.0-20260315 and proceed with canary now; B) abort canary window and wait for clean artifact rebuild. We prefer A for availability. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 
jas: Vote A. We can run quick smoke e2e against the pinned image and roll forward after fix.
akira: Vote A + run smoke. I'll run canary smoke suite and monitor metrics.
ci-bot: CI job re-run requested: `artifact-cleanup-and-smoke` by akira. Queue position 2.
marta: I'll still delete orphaned multipart parts and drop the bad manifest so future uploads don't pick it up. That should reduce recurrence.
release-manager: OK pinned. @theo can you trigger the deploy of release-2.3.0-20260315 to canary and add note in the release thread about the pin and cache incident? include rollback instructions.
theo: triggered. Deploybot confirmed canary start.
deploybot: Canary deployment started: release-2.3.0-20260315 -> canary (id: cb-3839001112). Smoke checks in progress.
akira: smoke passed first wave (latency and basic flows). watching for error budget and 5m traces.
jas: leaving a reminder: do NOT promote to prod until we have a clean artifact rebuild and verification. We'll add a ticket to track the cache restore fix.
release-manager: Adding ticket RN-512 to track: "cache-multipart-resume-causes-manifest-drift". We'll include incident note in release notes and mark the canary as pinned.
marta: FYI logs for artifact job: S3 503s coincided with a throttling window from the provider; I added exponential backoff and will run a canary job using a warm uploader bucket.
release-manager: Great work team. Marking this thread resolved for the immediate canary. Follow-up owners: @marta for uploader fix, @jas for verification and prod decision, @theo for rollout when green. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: job artifact-cleanup-and-smoke completed: success.
last: release-manager: Closing thread, will update release-notes with pinned tag and incident blurb.
